text:
alex: Heads-up — eu-central dedicated GPU pool (pool-eu-c-01) showing sudden node flaps, ~25/120 nodes NotReady. Autoscaler didn't respond, and smart-routing started spilling requests to hosted. Seeing ~2.8k req/min shift. Anyone grabbing this?

ops-oncall: I'm oncall, pulling logs. Initial look: repeated NIC resets and kubelet OOMs on a subset of 2 AZs. Marking affected nodes cordoned.

maria: Can we confirm if this is infra-level (host/driver) or kernel/kernel-module? If driver bug we might need a reboot/evac plan.

jin: From host metrics: kernel dmesg shows `i40e` resets (Intel NIC driver). A recent OS rollback last rollout window touched network driver updates on these images.

ops-oncall: Confirmed. `dmesg` dump: ```
[ 2412.123456] i40e 0000:3b:00.0 eth0: Reset adapter
[ 2412.123462] i40e 0000:3b:00.0 eth0: link down
[ 2412.223987] i40e 0000:3b:00.0 eth0: link up
[ 2412.224001] kubelet[1234]: evicting pods due to OOM```

alex: Ugh. That matches a vendor driver regression we saw in staging last month. Why didn't autoscaler respond?

ops-oncall: Autoscaler saw nodes NotReady but threshold policy is conservative (wait 5m to avoid thrash). Since flaps are frequent, autoscaler held. That allowed capacity to slip below SLO and triggered fallback to hosted.

maria: Good we have fallback, but cost and latency hit is noticeable. @finance FYI — hosted spend will spike while we remediate.

leila: Deploy-bot shows a canary patch to the node image was applied in eu-central at 03:12 UTC. Might be the culprit. Rolling back would require draining nodes which could worsen the immediate capacity shortfall.

jin: Proposed immediate actions: 1) Pause autoscaler cooldown to force small scale-up from unaffected hosts (increase desired to account for cordoned nodes) 2) Temporarily relax routing policy so only latency-sensitive routes go to hosted, others queue/batch in region 3) Begin targeted kernel-driver rollback on affected AZ (one AZ at a time)

ops-oncall: Implementing step 1 now: `kubectl patch --namespace=infra autoscaler scalingpolicy --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"cooldownSeconds":60}}'` — patch applied.

deploy-bot: Rollout-guard triggered: 5 nodes cordoned, 0/5 drained. Next rollout action blocked by manual approval.

maria: For step 2, I'll flip routing weights for eu-central in prod-router: reduce hosted fallback weight from 1.0 -> 0.6 for non-realtime routes. Doing that now.

alex: Good. Ops: start AZ-then-rollback on the image for the most impacted AZ (eu-central-1b). We'll avoid simultaneous reboots. Use `evacuate` runbook and set `sre-bot` alerts to high severity.

sre-bot: Alert: pool-eu-c-01 capacity at 76% degraded. Pager routed to ops-oncall, jin, maria.

ops-oncall: Starting targeted rollback on eu-central-1b images. Draining nodes one at a time, instance reboot + image rollback. ETA ~18-25m for first batch. Monitoring CPU/token latency.

jin: I'll watch kernel logs and host metrics. If flaps continue after rollback we escalate to host vendor.

maria: FYI the hosted fallback is adding ~40ms p50 on average for generation routes and cost per token ~1.6x vs dedicated. Putting a short note in #finance.

leila: Manual approval given for deploy-bot to proceed with rollback. Kicking it off for the 1b AZ.

ops-oncall: First 5 nodes drained and rolled back, coming back to Ready. Early signs: NIC resets stopped on those hosts. Host-level packet drops down from 12% -> 0.8%.

alex: Nice. Keep rolling through AZs, keep routing weight conservative until all AZs healthy. After full remediation let's audit the image pipeline change that slipped through.

maria: I'll open a postmortem ticket and tag image pipeline owners + vendor. Also propose lowering autoscaler cooldown only for dedicated pools that have fallback configured so we avoid unnecessary spillovers in future.

ops-oncall: Monitoring continues. Current hosted spill = -1.9k req/min down from +2.8k. Latency trending back to baseline. Will update in 15m or on completion. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks team. Great coordination.
